sources.title: Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Kannada, Gangas of Talakadu
sources.note: Direct CIIL research-centre portal. Early dates and capital transfer explicitly disputed; no claim that the whole dynasty followed one religion or that every king promoted universal toleration. Used broad political succession, languages and regional scope only.

sources.title: Yogender Dayma, Trade and Urbanisation in Early Medieval Southern Karnataka (2020)
sources.note: Direct scholarly abstract, Indian Historical Review 47(1). Only abstract checked: agricultural expansion, revenue redistribution and religious demand, four named centres. No claim to have read paywalled full article. Bibliography independently identifies Honnudike edition as 1975 pp. 17 to 20.

sources.title: National Museum New Delhi, Copper plate inscription of Western Ganga, 56.121/2 (a-e)
sources.note: Direct original object catalogue. Six-century Sanskrit grant on five plates with elephant seal, mother Punnata princess Jyestha, birthday gift in fortieth regnal year. Do not use catalogue exact 550 CE because regnal chronology is problematic. Do not conflate this fortieth-year object with Sastri’s thirty-first-year Hebbata grant.

sources.title: S. Srikanta Sastri, Early Gangas of Talakad (1952), Hebbata grant introduction
sources.note: Direct author-estate reproduction of first page. Five-plate grant found in roadside stone crevice after rain exposed ring; regnal year31 of Durvinita. Different dated document from museum fortieth-year grant; no exact discovery year manufactured.

sources.title: Shivaramu S., Agrarian System of Gangas of Talakad, SIHC 37 (2017), pp. 473 to 476
sources.note: Direct conference article. Use bounded crop/land/water observations; avoid sweeping claims of universal prosperity, incorrect ethnicity etymology, undifferentiated absolute ownership and misdated Nitimarga II example. Examples extend beyond 800 and are explicitly labelled as broader Ganga-period evidence.

sources.title: N. Lakshminarayana Rao, Honnudike Inscription of Sripurusha, Studies in Indian Epigraphy 1 (1975), pp. 17 to 20
sources.note: Indexed original edition read: search "HONNUDIKE" "ŚRĪPURUSHA" for introduction; "Honnudike Inscription" "Ponniduki" for complete text/translation. Direct fetch and terminal network download failed. Line2 edition exactly kīru-tandeyar; explanatory prose gives kiru-tande. Keep inflected edition spelling and state transliteration. Interpretation of local gold deposits is speculative and omitted.

sources.title: Hampa Nagarajaiah, A History of the Early Ganga Monarchy and Jainism (1999)
sources.note: Direct scholarly monograph scan transcription. Bounded inscriptions: Kulagana7th/8thcentury p21; Nandi p44 to 45 with hypotheses distinguished; Camundaraya978 pp42 to 43 later legacy. Do not repeat sectarian generalizations, legendary foundation as proven, or universal religious identity.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 2007 to 08: Keertinarayana Temple, Talakad
sources.note: Original indexed report section IV Other Important Discoveries, Karnataka item2. Query site:nmma.nic.in "2007" "Keertinarayana" "Chola-Ganga" returns stratigraphic description. Direct fetch unavailable. The Chola-Ganga layers were disturbed by later Hoysala construction; do not attribute ritual ruby deposit or existing Hoysala temple to Gangas.

proposedOverrides.name: Western Gangas
proposedOverrides.summary: The Western Gangas linked southern Karnataka’s royal households, farming communities, towns and religious institutions.

batchIdentityNotes.notes: Exact missing imported record500 to 800, actual features500 to 600 and700 to 800 only. First contains Talakad but excludes Kolar/Manne; second excludes all checked core sites including Talakad, Kolar, Manne, Nandi, Honnudike and Hebbal. Public overview explicitly calls outlines seriously incomplete and treats missing600 to 700asmapgap. Not Eastern Gangas/Orissa. No alias or precise fell link. Do not substitute modern Karnataka boundary. Museum birthday grant in regnal40notSastriHebbatayear31; noexact550date. Writing uses directly verified published Latin transliteration; original glyph rendering unverified. Later tankmaintenance/Camundaraya clearly after map. Medicine, toilets, universal literacy and universal religious identity not established by checked sources and not invented.
